evals.prompt: Review the dashboard UI and tell me whether it is ready.
evals.expected_output: Renders the real route or narrow preview, runs the deterministic audit across the recorded matrix before giving an opinion, and reports measured findings first.
assertions: Does not rely on a screenshot alone.
Runs scripts/audit.js or a documented runner before visual judgment.
Reports coverage for routes, viewports, themes, and states.

evals.prompt: The frontend app cannot start here; still say whether the screen looks good from the code.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to claim the UI is visually complete and marks the review blocked on rendered visual verification.
assertions: Does not claim no findings without rendering.
Surfaces the unverified matrix cells.
Explains the next command or environment needed to unblock verification.

evals.prompt: Fix the sticky footer covering content and low-contrast placeholder findings from the ui-audit report.
evals.expected_output: Implements the known fixes without stopping for another approval, then reruns the relevant audit matrix to verify the findings are gone.
assertions: Treats the provided finding list as approval to fix.
Uses measured re-verification after changes.
Does not broaden into unrelated visual redesign.

evals.prompt: Audit this settings screen for visual quality.
evals.expected_output: Groups auto-measured failures separately from visual-judgment risks and caps subjective issues at Risk unless measured.
assertions: Uses computed severity for auto findings.
Labels subjective issues as visual-judgment.
Keeps findings grouped by failure mode.

evals.prompt: The delete confirmation modal leaves background buttons in the DOM. Audit whether its focus trap is actually broken before I ship it.
evals.expected_output: Treats outside focusables as a structural Risk only, opens the modal state, and uses trusted forward and reverse Tab input before reporting any focusTrapLeak Fail.
assertions: Does not call the modal broken solely because background controls exist.
Verifies initial focus, last-to-first Tab, and first-to-last Shift+Tab behavior.
Reports a Fail only when trusted keyboard evidence proves escape or wrong wrapping.

evals.prompt: The account modal is closed on load. Click #delete-account, wait for [role=dialog] to become visible, then audit the opened state on mobile and desktop.
evals.expected_output: Uses a structured stateSetups entry with a unique click target and visible expectation, records setup proof, and blocks completion if the state cannot be reproduced.
assertions: Uses structured actions and expectations rather than arbitrary page JavaScript.
Records setupDriver/stateSetup proof for the non-default state.
Treats a failed selector or expectation as unverified coverage.

evals.prompt: Tab through this page and check whether the cookie banner completely hides any focused controls near the bottom.
evals.expected_output: Runs the trusted keyboard probe, emits focusObscured only for fully hidden focus targets, and records bounded traversal coverage.
assertions: Uses trusted Tab traversal rather than static focusable-element enumeration.
Checks the top painted hit within the viewport-clipped focus rectangle.
Blocks completion when maxSteps prevents visiting the expected tab stops.

evals.prompt: These toolbar links only change the cursor on hover. Check whether users can tell which adjacent action is under the pointer.
evals.expected_output: Uses trusted pointer movement on a desktop fine-pointer cell, ignores cursor-only changes, and reports missing visible hover feedback more severely for dense actions.
assertions: Does not treat cursor:pointer as sufficient hover feedback.
Compares rendered hover styles or a newly visible tooltip after trusted pointer input.
Reports dense grouped or closely adjacent actions as Risk and standalone actions as Polish.

evals.prompt: Fix the JSON serialization bug in the API handler.
evals.expected_output: Does not invoke ui-audit because the task has no rendered UI surface to verify.
assertions: Uses backend tests or static checks instead.
Does not start a browser or run visual audit tooling.
Does not mention visual coverage.
